title: What the Output Does When Nothing Is in Charge: Safe Values per Channel and a Brake That Applies on Loss of Power

questions.question: The controller dies. What does an output stage do with a channel if nobody chose?
options: Sets it to zero, which is what a dead controller would send
Sets it to a safe value from its data sheet
Switches the channel off and raises a fault
Holds the last command, which for a motor at 80 percent is the opposite of a stop
questions.explanation: Unless told otherwise an output stage keeps doing the last thing it was told. For a drive motor that means carrying on.

questions.question: Five channels left on hold: which were unsafe when the controller died?
options: All five, since none had a policy
drive_left, drive_right, steering and brake_coil; the horn was at its safe value (0) and is fine
Only the two drives, which move the robot
None: hold is a safe default
questions.explanation: A channel is unsafe if it ends somewhere other than its safe value. The horn was already off, so holding it changed nothing.

questions.question: Why was an ESC channel unsafe on the zero policy?
options: Its neutral is a 1500 us pulse, and a pulse of 0 is no signal, which the ESC may treat as anything
Its pulse must be at least 1000 us, and zero is below that
An ESC needs 24 V and zero volts switches it off
Zero is the ESC's full reverse
questions.explanation: A pulse of zero width is the absence of a signal. What a speed controller does then is up to its maker, so the channel needs its own safe value, 1500.

questions.question: With the robot moving, how many of the four failures engaged a spring applied brake, and a power applied one?
options: 4 and 4: any brake engages when something fails
0 and 3: the power applied brake is the one that acts
3 and 0: for the spring, a lost supply, a cut wire and a dead controller driving zero are the command to stop
2 and 2
questions.explanation: A spring holds the brake on unless a coil is powered. Loss of supply, a cut wire and a zero output all remove the power, so they are stops. A power applied brake needs all three to work.

questions.question: What closes the case of an output stage that holds the coil at 24 V?
options: A stronger spring in the brake
A second brake of the power applied kind
Nothing can: the spring cannot overcome a driven coil
A safe-value policy on the coil channel (0 V), so the stage drives the coil to where the spring applies the brake
questions.explanation: The coil is a channel like any other, with a safe value of 0 V. With the stage set to drive it there on failure, the spring applies the brake in all four cases.

questions.question: How is the real behaviour of an output stage found?
options: By killing the controller on the bench and watching the output: the model is as true as the data sheet it came from
By reading the data sheet, which is always right
By asking the application what it last sent
By checking that the model's tests pass
questions.explanation: The model says what the data sheet says. Whether the real stage holds, zeros or does something else is found by killing the controller and measuring.
